You’ll join a global team while establishing the technical Support Engineering presence in APAC, with the ownership and visibility that come from being its first Support Engineer in the region. We staff across regions rather than relying on on-call rotations; we’ll discuss the specific schedule for this opening during the process. Not sure which Support role is right for you? We’re hiring for both Product Support Specialist and Product Support Engineer roles. Support Specialist owns cases and customer communication end-to-end. Troubleshoots complex issues by navigating internal tooling — audit logs, user experience testing, and API testing — to help customers reach successful outcomes. Support Engineering serves as the escalation point between Support Specialists and Product Engineering. Owns integrations, supports data mapping and data migrations for customers, and resolves escalated tickets that don't require product code changes. Please choose the role that best reflects your experience and interests rather than applying to both. If another Support role seems like a closer match, we’ll consider that in our review. About The Role Support Engineering is the technical layer between frontline Support and Engineering. You’ll take on complex issues involving integrations, APIs, permissions, data, reporting, migrations, and workflows—using application behavior, logs, databases, and customer context to determine whether an issue can be resolved through Support or represents a product defect. You’ll investigate issues end to end using tools such as Plain, GitHub, Datadog, databases, and the codebase. You won’t write the fix; you’ll give Engineering a well-validated escalation with reproduction steps, relevant evidence, customer impact, and a root-cause hypothesis when possible. You’ll also identify recurring issues, improve documentation and enablement, and partner with Product and Engineering on improvements. As Ashby’s first Support Engineer in APAC, you’ll help define how the global team collaborates across time zones, build practical handoffs with EMEA and AMER, and bring APAC customer context into how we scale Support Engineering. What You’ll Own Own complex technical issues from intake through resolution or escalation, investigating APIs, integrations, logs, data, configuration, and workflows to determine whether Support can resolve them or Engineering should be involved. Set a high bar for complex technical investigations and ensure Engineering receives clear, actionable, well-validated product issues. Build trusted working relationships with frontline Support, Engineering, Product, Customer Success, and customers. Identify recurring problems and turn them into documentation, enablement, tooling, process improvements, or product feedback. Partner with Product and Engineering on recurring product improvements by synthesizing customer patterns, validating defects, and sharing the technical context needed to choose between a product change, documentation, tooling, or process improvement. Build the APAC coverage and handoff model with teammates in EMEA and AMER, while bringing regional customer patterns to the global Support Engineering team. Track and improve the outcomes that matter: resolution speed, escalation quality, fewer avoidable Engineering escalations, frontline self-sufficiency, reduced customer effort, and customer confidence. You Should Apply If You’ve worked in a hands-on, customer-centric technical role where you independently investigate ambiguous issues involving APIs, integrations, logs, data, and application behavior. You’re comfortable moving between customer conversations, APIs, logs, databases, product behavior, and code-level context to find root causes. You can distinguish a configuration, data, documentation, or enablement issue from a true product defect—and explain your reasoning clearly. You write precise investigations that others can quickly understand and act on, and communicate thoughtfully with technical and non-technical audiences across time zones. You naturally look beyond the immediate ticket and improve the systems around it through documentation, enablement, tooling, or process design. You want to be the first technical owner for APAC and are energized by building structure across a broad set of time zones within a global team. You Should Not Apply If You’re looking primarily for a high-volume support role centered on predefined troubleshooting steps, rather than open-ended technical investigation and ownership. Most of your experience is in internal IT, help desk, endpoint, hardware, network, infrastructure, cloud operations, systems administration, infrastructure maintenance, or service deployment—and you haven’t worked extensively with customer-centric SaaS applications, APIs, logs, or data-backed troubleshooting. You prefer to pass difficult issues to another team rather than reproduce, investigate, and explain them yourself. You’re looking for a role focused mainly on writing production code; this role diagnoses and escalates bugs but does not own code changes. You prefer clear-cut problems and predefined answers over working through ambiguity with careful documentation, focused questions, and evidence-based decisions. You want a narrowly defined role without regional operating ownership or projects that improve how the broader Support team works. About Ashby Ashby builds a suite of products that helps talent leaders, recruiters, and hiring managers run their hiring process significantly better. We raised a $50M Series D in July 2025 and support nearly 5,000 customers, including Shopify, Snowflake, OpenAI, Deliveroo, and Confluent. We’re growing much faster than 100% year over year, with a team of roughly 300 people across 22+ countries. Learn more at ashbyhq.com. About Go To Market We view our Support team as an extension of the product itself, one that ensures an optimal customer experience for customers ranging across all market segments. Here are a few points that should give you an idea of what it is like to work with us: We spend a lot of time building best-in-class products since we believe a highly differentiated product is easier to sell. We also spend a lot of time building a best-in-class customer experience. We aim to offer deep expertise whenever we interact with prospects and customers. We strongly believe that small teams with very talented people and the right work environment deliver much better performance than teams with large headcount. We value a strong sense of ownership, principled thinking over experience, and thoughtful communication (we put a lot of effort into using the right communication channels) - we’ll get into these and other values during the hiring process. You can take a look at our Leadership Principles to get a sense of what we value in People Leaders at Ashby. Interview process Our interview process is thorough and designed to give you enough information to assess whether Ashby is the right fit for you, while helping us evaluate technical reasoning, communication precision, and ownership. Intro call with Recruiting — 30 min Take-home assessment — 5 days to complete Hiring Manager interview — 45–60 min Virtual onsite — 120 min Meet the team — 30 min Technical & integration skills — 45 min CS and Support leadership — 30 min Closing questions — 15 min Onboarding Your onboarding will combine Ashby-wide product and company training with a Support Engineering-specific ramp plan. You’ll learn the product and support workflow, get familiar with the tools and systems used for technical investigations, and build relationships across Support, Product, and Engineering. With support from your manager and onboarding buddy, you’ll take on increasingly complex investigations as you build context, with regular check-ins throughout your first 90 days. Benefits Benefits vary by country and are shared in more detail during the process. International employees receive statutory benefits and, where available, employer-paid supplemental health coverage. 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby —do it when you feel financially comfortable. Unlimited PTO. review_candidates.description: CHIEF FINANCIAL OFFICER (CFO) — CAPITAL & PROJECT FINANCE Kamen Construction Limited | Abuja, Nigeria | Full-Time About Kamen Kamen Construction Limited is a Nigerian infrastructure development and construction company delivering roads, drainage, water, electrical infrastructure, buildings and other integrated infrastructure solutions. Through  Kamen Infrastructure Development Services (KAMEN-IDS) , Kamen is developing a structured infrastructure delivery and financing platform that enables governments, real estate developers, corporate organisations, communities and private clients to deliver infrastructure through flexible financing arrangements. As we enter our next phase of growth, we are seeking a commercially driven and highly capable  Chief Financial Officer (CFO)  to lead our financial strategy, capital raising, project finance, investment structuring, treasury and financial governance. This is  not a conventional accounting-focused CFO position . We are looking for a finance leader who can help build Kamen's financial architecture, raise equity and debt, establish project SPVs, structure infrastructure transactions and develop strong relationships with banks, investors, capital houses and institutional funding partners. The Role The CFO will be a key member of Kamen's executive management team and will report directly to the Managing Director/CEO. The successful candidate will lead the company's corporate finance strategy while serving as the financial champion for  KAMEN-IDS and its project-financing platform . The role combines corporate finance, capital raising, project finance, treasury, investment management and financial governance. Key Responsibilities 1. Corporate Finance & Strategy Develop and execute Kamen's financial strategy and capital structure. Lead budgeting, forecasting, financial modelling and capital allocation. Provide the CEO and Board with financial and strategic decision support. Improve profitability, cash generation and return on invested capital. Establish strong financial controls, policies and governance. 2. Capital Raising & Investor Relations Develop and execute Kamen's equity and debt capital-raising strategy. Identify and build relationships with private equity funds, infrastructure funds, family offices, banks, development finance institutions, institutional investors, private credit funds and capital-market operators. Prepare investment teasers, information memoranda, financial models and investor presentations. Lead investor discussions, due diligence and transaction negotiations. Build and manage a pipeline of potential investors and financing partners. Lead successful equity investment transactions for Kamen and its projects. 3. KAMEN-IDS Project Finance & SPVs Develop the financial architecture for KAMEN-IDS. Establish and manage appropriate Project Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs). Structure project-level financing and determine the appropriate mix of equity, debt, client contributions, supplier credit and other funding sources. Develop detailed project financial models covering construction costs, cash flow, revenues, financing costs, profitability, IRR, DSCR, payback and sensitivity analysis. Assess the bankability of projects before financial commitment. Coordinate financial close and project-financing processes. Ensure project funds are appropriately ring-fenced and controlled. Monitor the financial performance of project SPVs. 4. Debt, Debentures & Structured Finance Lead Kamen's debt-financing initiatives. Develop relationships with banks, investment firms, capital houses and private credit providers. Structure and negotiate corporate loans, project finance, debentures, private debt, asset-backed financing, receivables-backed financing, bridge financing and other structured-finance facilities. Negotiate financing terms including pricing, tenor, security, covenants and repayment structures. Coordinate lender due diligence and financial documentation. 5. Treasury & Cash Flow Lead Kamen's treasury function and group-wide cash management. Establish rolling cash-flow forecasts and liquidity controls. Optimise working capital and cash conversion. Manage banking relationships and financing facilities. Ensure proper utilisation of project funds and timely debt servicing. Establish early-warning indicators for liquidity and financial risk. 6. Financial Reporting, Risk & Governance Lead the Finance & Accounts function and ensure accurate and timely management reporting. Strengthen budgeting, variance analysis, receivables and payables management. Coordinate audits, tax compliance and statutory reporting. Develop financial risk-management and internal-control systems. Ensure effective financial governance across Kamen and its project SPVs. 7. Leadership Build and lead a high-performance Finance, Treasury, Investment and Capital Management team. Establish clear KPIs and accountability. Work closely with Projects, Commercial, Procurement, Business Development and Operations to ensure projects are commercially viable and properly funded. Key Performance Measures The CFO will be measured primarily by business outcomes, including: Equity capital successfully raised. Debt and debenture financing successfully secured. Number and value of financing transactions closed. Capital raised for KAMEN-IDS projects. Number of project SPVs established and financed. Successful financial closes. Cost and structure of capital achieved. Project profitability and return on capital. Cash-flow and liquidity performance. Quality of investor and lender relationships. Strength of financial controls and reporting. Qualifications & Experience Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business Administration or related discipline. Professional qualification such as  ACA, ACCA, CFA, CIMA  or equivalent. Minimum  10–15 years' relevant experience , including substantial senior-management experience. Proven experience in corporate finance, project finance, investment banking, structured finance or infrastructure financing. Demonstrable experience raising equity and/or debt capital. Strong financial-modelling and transaction-structuring skills. Experience negotiating with banks, investors and capital providers. Strong understanding of Nigerian financial and capital markets. Experience in  construction, infrastructure, real estate, private equity, private credit, development finance or investment banking  will be highly advantageous. The Ideal Candidate We are looking for a  builder, not just a financial controller . The ideal candidate must be commercially astute, entrepreneurial, analytical and highly skilled in financial modelling, deal structuring and negotiation. He or she should be comfortable engaging CEOs, investors, fund managers, bankers, government stakeholders and other sophisticated capital providers. Most importantly, candidates must demonstrate  actual transactions completed , not simply experience preparing financial reports. Candidates who have personally led or materially contributed to successful equity raises, debt transactions, debentures, project-finance deals or investment transactions will have a significant advantage. Our Expectation Within the first 12–18 months, the CFO should help Kamen transition from a predominantly construction-company financing model toward an  institutional infrastructure-financing platform , capable of: Originate → Structure → Finance → Execute → Monitor → Recycle Capital across a growing portfolio of infrastructure projects. Application Interested candidates should submit a detailed CV highlighting their experience in  capital raising, corporate finance, project finance, investment banking, debt/equity transactions, and infrastructure financing . Candidates should clearly identify significant transactions they have personally led or materially contributed to, including the approximate value and nature of each transaction.
